A.notes: Recommends polling + Redis cache scheduled refresh, explicitly rejecting SSE/WebSocket/Kafka as overkill for a 30s demo cadence. Proportional to the timeline, names Kafka only as long-term direction. Slight extra infra (Redis) but justified for demo load stability; asks clarifying questions rather than asserting.

B.notes: Leanest answer ('bicycle version'): single GROUP BY endpoint, no new infra, with optional materialized view. Flags Kafka as an alternative for the 'modern architecture' story without making it primary. Well-calibrated, demo-appropriate, surfaces the monolith-extraction concern honestly.

C.notes: Presents simple vs. new analytics-service options but tilts toward the heavier Kafka/Redis service, calling it 'strategically valuable' for investor optics â€” drifts into over-engineering for a one-week demo. The optics framing biases away from the proportional choice, though it does acknowledge the timeline risk.

analysis: All three correctly anchor on the monolith/PostgreSQL reality and a polling approach, but they differ in proportionality. B is the most calibrated: minimal endpoint, no new infrastructure, Kafka mentioned only as an optional future story. A is nearly as strong, explicitly enumerating why SSE/WebSocket/Kafka are overkill, though it adds a Redis cache layer that is slightly more than a demo strictly needs. C is the weakest on bias resistance: it frames a Kafka-backed analytics-service as 'strategically valuable' for investor optics and leans toward it, edging into the over-engineering trap the scenario warns against, despite flagging the timeline risk. Hence B > A > C.
